construction.note: This is the standard eight-pointed star made from two squares in a circle, repeated on a tangent square. No specific published teaching sequence is claimed.
construction.changes: The Kashan tile photograph was used to check the finished pattern. It is a historical reference, not a set of construction instructions.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Put the compass point on the centre and draw a circle.
Draw a horizontal line through the centre, then a vertical line at right angles to it. They cut the circle at four points.
Halve each right angle to get the two diagonals. The circle is now divided into eight equal parts.
Join the four points on the horizontal and vertical lines. This is the dynamic square, standing on its corner.
Join the four points on the diagonals. This is the static square, sitting flat. The two squares cross each other at eight points.
Draw the square that just touches the circle: a line at right angles to the horizontal at each side, and at right angles to the vertical at the top and bottom. This square is the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Go over the outline of the two squares, turning at every crossing. You get an eight-point star.

pattern.text: Repeat the tile edge to edge, with the same star in every square. Neighbouring stars touch at their points, and the space between four stars closes into a cross.

expect.note: Golden values, in units of OA. Checked numerically with the prototype's arrangement code.
